full_judgment: 4. The facts relevant for disposal of the Rule as stated in the Writ Petition are that the land measuring 0.27 acre pertaining to SA Plot No. 2347 under SA Khatian No. 28 corresponding to BS Plot No. 2049 of Mouza-Dottorail, JL No. 62 Police Station, Golapganj, Sylhet (the suit land) has been included in the 'Ka' schedule of vested property list published in serial No. 179 in Bangladesh Gazette Notification dated 19-4-2012. The petitioner as plaintiff on 2-1-2013 filed Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Suit No. 23 of 2013 before the Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Additional Tribunal No. 3, Sylhet for releasing the suit land from the 'K' list of vested property contending, inter alia, that one Moin Charan Shil of Village Dottorail, Golapganj, Sylhet was the original owner of the suit land. Said Moin Charan Shil sold the suit land to Abdul Latif, the predecessor of the petitioner through an unregistered Kabala dated 20-4-1963 on receiving Taka 95 as the consideration of the suit land and delivered possession thereof in his favour. After purchasing the suit land said Abdul Latif constructed a homestead therein. Abdul Latif died leaving behind two sons, namely Mujibur Rahman and Md Ziaur Rahman and three daughters namely Shahida Ali, Wahida Ahmed and Farida Latif as his legal heirs. Subsequently, among the legal heirs of said Abdul Latif the petitioner got exclusive title and possession over the suit land. The petitioner in a formidable circumstances took lease of the suit land in order to maintain his possession. The sole defendant, Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet contested the suit by filing a written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable and the suit land has been leased out to the petitioner vide VP Case No. 83 of 1969-70 as the original owner of the suit land left for India leaving the suit land uncared for and the Government became the lawful owner in the suit land and the suit is liable to be dismissed. The Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Additional Tribunal No.3, Sylhet after hearing the parties dismissed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 19-11-2005. The petitioner having been aggrieved by the said judgment and decree dated 19-11-2015 passed by the Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Additional Tribunal No.3, Sylhet moved the appellate forum by filing Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Appeal No. 11 of 2016 wherein the appeal is still pending.
